repository.description: Where newer versions of it are: a GitHub repository (one repository may hold many plugins, each in a folder with its own zeff-plugin.json and version). Plugins → Sources checks it and updates on a click.

path.description: The plugin's folder in the repository (empty: its top).

apiVersion.description: The extension API version it was written for (this Zeff speaks up to 1).

permissions.description: What it may do (granted by you): exec, network, prompt, and the permissions plugins bring (work.read, todos.write, workspace.write …).

workerRules.description: Text files whose content is added to the rules of every Code worker. Needs the prompt permission.

workCommands.description: Entries of the Code message box's "/" menu.

template.description: The text put into the message box when picked. May contain line breaks.

workerMcpServers.description: MCP servers every Code worker gets (stdio: needs exec; http: needs network).

command.description: The program. "node" is the Node that runs Zeff; "./x" is relative to the plugin folder.

workPanels.description: Views in Code, shown in a sandboxed frame.

entry.description: The panel's HTML page, relative to the plugin's ui/ folder.

placement.description: "tab": a view of its own, linked in Code's sidebar. "session": a drawer beside a session, which gets that session's ids.

apps.description: Entries in Zeff's menu (Apps) that open one of its panels as a page of its own — you can put them in the header (Menu → Customize).

panel.description: The id of one of the plugin's panels (workPanels) this entry opens.

short.description: Its name in the header, when you put it there.

hint.description: A line under the name in the menu.

hooks.description: Programs Zeff runs when something happens. Needs the exec permission.

command.description: Program and arguments, no shell. "node" is the Node that runs Zeff; "./x" is relative to the plugin folder.

flowActions.description: Actions for flows (the Studio's and the AI's catalog): each is done by one of the plugin's functions. A flow that uses one needs the permission to call that function.

summary.description: What it does — the Studio shows it and the AI reads it when it builds a flow.

function.description: The plugin function (contributes.functions) that does it: its arguments are the action's input, its result the action's output.

writes.description: It changes something: a dry run of a flow does not call it.

fieldTypes.description: Field types for the Workspace's databases: an entry is checked (a pattern, a number range or a list of choices) and drawn as text, stars, a bar, a badge or a link. No code needed.

href.description: A link's address with {value} in it.

kind.description: What an entry is: any text (checked by `pattern`), a number (between `min` and `max`) or one of `options`.

pattern.description: A regular expression a text entry must match.

schedules.description: Functions run on their own, every so often, for every account the plugin is on in (upkeep, reminders, syncs). They do only what the user granted them.

function.description: The plugin function that is run.

everyMinutes.description: How often (5 minutes to a week), as long as Zeff is running and the plugin is on.

args.description: The arguments it is called with.

chats.description: Kinds of live chat with an agent in Zeff: its own rules, tools and a conversation kept in a database (a teacher, a coach, a reviewer).

rules.description: A text file with the agent's rules. {{name}} is replaced by what the context function gives (a list becomes lines); {{key}}, {{plugin}} and {{chat}} are always there.

context.description: The plugin function that gives the values for the rules, called with { key } each time a session starts.

tools.description: Zeff's MCP tools the agent may use beside the chat's own (workspace_call_function calls the plugin's functions).

conversation.description: Keep the conversation in a database the person can edit: what is changed there is what the agent goes on with.

database.description: The database that keeps the conversation, one row per message: its id, or its place in the plugin's package (@my-pkg.i9).

text.description: The field with the message's text (the row's title column is a short form of it).

role.description: A choice field for who said it.

roles.description: The names of the choices in that field: the person, the agent ("teacher", "coach" …), what happened on the side.

key.description: The field that tells which key (which lesson, ticket …) the message belongs to.

kind.description: A choice field for the kind of message: "message" for what is said, and the kinds `watch` names.

watch.description: Calls of the plugin's functions that are messages of their own, in the kind named (an exercise made, a step mastered): { function, kind, field? } — `field` is the argument whose value is the message's text.

lookups.description: Lookups for views (<lookup>: a film, a book …): a search and a details function of the plugin.

id.description: How a template names it: <plugin id>.<this>.

what.description: One line: what it finds (the AI reads it).

fields.description: The fields a hit has: name → what it is.

search.description: The plugin function that searches: gets { query, language }, gives back a list of { id, title, subtitle?, image? }.

details.description: The plugin function that reads one hit: gets { id, language }, gives back its fields by name (text, number, list of texts or null).

sources.description: Data sources for the pipelines: a database can follow one; a function of the plugin reads its records.

hint.description: One line: what the records are.

read.description: The plugin function that reads the records: gives back a list of { ref, title, key?, fields?, text?, url?, updatedAt? }.

noNewRows.description: The records are only read from where they live: a row cannot be made by hand.

functions.description: Server functions of its own: code (Python or Node.js) that runs in the Notebook's sessions and is called over HTTP (POST /api/ext/fn/<plugin>/<name>), from Notebook cells (zeff.call) and by other functions.

name.description: Its name: how it is called (plugin id + this).

runtime.description: The language of its file: it runs like a Notebook cell, in a Docker container (or on this computer), by the Notebook plugin.

file.description: Its code, relative to the plugin folder. The arguments arrive as `inputs` (and as variables); what it returns — its last expression, or a top-level return — is the result.

input.description: The arguments it takes: name → what it is (documentation).

needs.description: What of Zeff its code reads or changes through zeff.* (tables, metrics, outputs, databases, database:<id>, write:outputs, write:database:<id>, delete:database:<id>, meta:…, call:<plugin>.<name>): you grant them for the function in Settings → Notebook; without them the call is refused.

webhook.description: Programs outside Zeff may call it: POST /api/ext/hook/<plugin>/<name> with a secret you make in Settings → Notebook (only the functions that say so).

formulaFunctions.description: Functions for formulas (views, formula fields, tables): each a formula of its own, called by its name like Zeff's own (a name Zeff or another plugin has already is left out).

args.description: Its arguments, by name — read in `value` as prop("name").

value.description: What it gives: a formula of Zeff's formula language, its arguments as prop("name") — no code, nothing it can change.

what.description: One line: what it gives (the formula help and the AI read it).

metrics.description: Kennzahlen: numbers a plugin function gives, kept and asked again when they are older than everyMinutes.

label.description: Its name as a Kennzahl (formulas read it with kennzahl("…")).

function.description: The plugin function that gives the number (called with {}); its last answer is what the Kennzahl shows.

everyMinutes.description: How old its last answer may be before it is asked again (in the background).

appViews.description: App views for the databases of a type (a mail client for mails): a template of the view language each, made the database's view.

dataType.description: The databases of this type get it (as their first view when Zeff makes one, and in the View menu): "mail", "message", "inbox" …

template.description: Its view template (the view language), a file in the plugin.

rowBadges.description: Badges on the rows its sources brought (by their refs), given by a plugin function.

prefix.description: The rows its sources brought (by their record's ref) it puts badges on.

function.description: The plugin function that gives the badges: { "film:12": [{ "label": "2 new", "tone": "warn" }] }.

tabMenus.description: The menu of a tab (its address): entries a plugin function gives.

tab.description: The tab (by its address, "/my-app") whose menu it fills.

function.description: The plugin function that gives the entries: [{ href, label, hint? }].

widgets.description: Widgets for pages and the dashboard (New block → widget): a list, figures or one figure, given by a plugin function, with buttons that run another.

replaces.description: A built-in widget's id this one takes over (a port): its id is that one then, so the widgets on your pages go on working; while the built-in is there, the built-in's counts.

optionsFrom.description: A select's options from Zeff: "series" — the daily series you may see (your databases' fields first).

lambda.description: Or one of its lambdas (kind function), called the same way — no Notebook needed.

function.description: The plugin function that gives its data, called with { config }: { "kind": "list", "items": [{ id, text, detail?, meta?, href?, badge?, tone?, done?, actions? }] }, { "kind": "stats", "tiles": [{ label, value, detail?, tone?, href? }] } or { "kind": "figure", value, caption, detail?, href? }.

actLambda.description: Or one of its lambdas for the buttons.

act.description: The plugin function a button of it runs, called with { action, payload, config }; what it gives (data as above) is shown, else the data is read again.

pageNav.description: Entries under its pages in the Workspace tree, given by a plugin function.

function.description: The plugin function that gives entries under pages in the Workspace tree: [{ pageId, entries: [{ id, label, icon?, n?, group?, href? }] }].

reviewSources.description: Things that wait for your word in the review queue, listed and decided by plugin functions.

id.description: Its id: <plugin id>-<this> in the review queue.

list.description: The plugin function that gives what waits for a word: [{ id, title, detail?, confidence?, href?, actions: [{ id, label, primary? }] }].

act.description: The plugin function a button runs, called with { item, action }; what it gives (a text) is said.

services.description: Places of the kernel it fills (web.search …): what Zeff calls stays the same, this plugin answers.

name.description: A service of the kernel (lib/kernel/contract.ts KERNEL_SERVICES).

lambda.description: Its lambda (kind function) that answers in the service's shape.

compute.description: A script of pure functions its views run in the browser (<data compute="<plugin>.<fn>">): it defines ZeffCompute = { fn(input) }; input is the view's rows, fields, state, extras and with=. It runs in a sandboxed frame of its own — no network, nothing of Zeff.

lambdas.description: A folder of lambdas (<name>/lambda.json and its code, _lib.mjs shared): lookups and functions that run without the Notebook, each in a Node process of its own with only the domains and Zeff calls it names. Their secrets are the plugin's settings they name.

tools.description: Tools for the AI (Zeff's MCP, the Workspace chat, agents), each done by a plugin function — beside Zeff's own.

name.description: Its name among Zeff's tools — one Zeff or another plugin already has is left out.

description.description: What it does and when the AI should use it — the AI reads only this.

function.description: The plugin function that does it: called with the arguments; what it returns is the answer (text, or JSON).

lambda.description: Or one of its lambdas (contributes.lambdas, kind function) — runs without the Notebook: a Node process of its own, only the domains it names.

readOnly.description: It only reads: the AI may call it without asking where its tools are limited to reading.

settings.description: What the user sets for it (Plugins → its Settings): texts, numbers, choices and secrets (kept encrypted). Its functions get them as `inputs.zeffSettings`.

kind.description: secret: kept encrypted, never shown again once saved (an API key).

reviewLinks.description: Things waiting on a page of their own: the review queue shows how many and links there.

href.description: Where the things waiting are (inside Zeff).

count.description: The plugin function that gives how many wait (a number).

workspacePackages.description: Workspace apps it brings: package files (JSON — a page exported with its databases, widgets, flows), offered under New → templates and made with one click.

locales.description: Its texts in other languages: per language code a JSON file { "English text": "translation" } — for its views, blocks, pages and messages (English is the text itself). Zeff's own texts win where both have one.

language.description: A language pack: the language its locales file for this code makes Zeff speak (Settings → Language offers it while the plugin is installed).
